sections.title: The letter ó
paragraphs: The letter (ó) /ɔ/ sounds like the start of (olho) /ˈɔ.ʎu/, which means eye. This letter makes four different sounds.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, pull your tongue back, make a small circle with your lips, and raise your tongue high. For the second, lower your jaw and open your lips wide. For the third, keep your jaw mid height and round your lips. For the fourth, let air flow through both your nose and mouth. Put a finger before your nose to feel the warm air.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: In an unstressed syllable, it sounds like (obrigado) /u.bɾiˈɡa.du/. In a stressed syllable, it can sound open as in (avó) /ɐˈvɔ/, or close as in (avô) /ɐˈvo/. An accent mark shows the open or close sound. Before the letters m or n, or with a tilde, it becomes a nasal sound, as heard in (bom) /bõ/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not make a diphthong like the vowel sound in English boat. A diphthong has two vowel sounds in one syllable. Keep your lips and tongue still until the sound ends. At the end of a word, do not say the open sound from English lot. Say it like the vowel in English boot instead.
